title: Boss: controllers in code
summary: Selectors with expressions, rollout arithmetic and DaemonSet placement.

steps.title: The scene
body: - { key: tier, operator: In, values: [web, api] }
All parts must hold. `In` needs the key present with one of the values; `NotIn` passes if the key is absent or its value is not listed; `Exists` / `DoesNotExist` check only the key.

steps.title: matchExpressions
prompt: Write `bool Expr(Dictionary<string, string> labels, string key, string op, string[] values)` for the four operators `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, `DoesNotExist`.
Then `bool MatchAll(Dictionary<string, string> labels, List<(string Key, string Op, string[] Values)> exprs)`: true when every expression holds.
starter: bool Expr(Dictionary<string, string> labels, string key, string op, string[] values)
bool MatchAll(Dictionary<string, string> labels, List<(string Key, string Op, string[] Values)> exprs)
solution: bool Expr(Dictionary<string, string> labels, string key, string op, string[] values)
bool has = labels.TryGetValue(key, out var v);
bool MatchAll(Dictionary<string, string> labels, List<(string Key, string Op, string[] Values)> exprs)
return exprs.All(e => Expr(labels, e.Key, e.Op, e.Values));
template: Dojo.Check("missing key In is false", !Expr(dojoL, "zone", "In", new[] { "a" }), "");
Dojo.Check("missing key NotIn is true", Expr(dojoL, "zone", "NotIn", new[] { "a" }), "");
Dojo.Check("MatchAll example", MatchAll(dojoL, new() { ("tier", "In", new[] { "web", "api" }), ("env", "NotIn", new[] { "dev" }), ("canary", "DoesNotExist", Array.Empty<string>()) }), "");
Dojo.Check("MatchAll fails when one fails", !MatchAll(dojoL, new() { ("tier", "In", new[] { "web" }), ("app", "DoesNotExist", Array.Empty<string>()) }), "");
hints: Start with `bool has = labels.TryGetValue(key, out var v);`.
A `switch` expression on `op` keeps it to four lines.

steps.title: Resolve maxSurge and maxUnavailable
prompt: In YAML the knobs can be a number (`"1"`) or a percentage (`"25%"`). Write `(int Surge, int Unavailable) Resolve(int replicas, string maxSurge, string maxUnavailable)`. Percentages of `replicas`: surge rounds **up**, unavailable rounds **down**. If both resolve to 0, Kubernetes would never make progress, so set unavailable to 1.
starter: (int Surge, int Unavailable) Resolve(int replicas, string maxSurge, string maxUnavailable)
solution: int Part(int replicas, string value, bool roundUp)
(int Surge, int Unavailable) Resolve(int replicas, string maxSurge, string maxUnavailable)
hints: Write a helper that handles one value with a `roundUp` flag.

steps.title: Place a DaemonSet
prompt: A DaemonSet with a `nodeSelector` runs one pod on each node whose labels match it. Nodes with the taint `NoSchedule` are skipped unless the DaemonSet tolerates it.

Write `List<string> DaemonPods(string ds, Dictionary<string, string> nodeSelector, bool toleratesNoSchedule, List<(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> Labels, bool Tainted)> nodes)` returning `"ds-on-nodename"` for each node that gets a pod, in node order.
starter: List<string> DaemonPods(string ds, Dictionary<string, string> nodeSelector, bool toleratesNoSchedule, List<(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> Labels, bool Tainted)> nodes)
solution: List<string> DaemonPods(string ds, Dictionary<string, string> nodeSelector, bool toleratesNoSchedule, List<(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> Labels, bool Tainted)> nodes)
.Where(n => nodeSelector.All(kv => n.Labels.TryGetValue(kv.Key, out var v) && v == kv.Value))
template: var dojoNodes = new List<(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> Labels, bool Tainted)> {
Dojo.Eq("linux, no toleration", new List<string> { "logs-on-n1", "logs-on-n2" }, DaemonPods("logs", new() { ["os"] = "linux" }, false, dojoNodes));
Dojo.Eq("linux, tolerates control plane", new List<string> { "cni-on-cp-1", "cni-on-n1", "cni-on-n2" }, DaemonPods("cni", new() { ["os"] = "linux" }, true, dojoNodes));
Dojo.Eq("gpu only", new List<string> { "gpu-on-n1" }, DaemonPods("gpu", new() { ["gpu"] = "true" }, false, dojoNodes));
Dojo.Eq("no selector, no toleration", new List<string> { "x-on-n1", "x-on-n2", "x-on-w1" }, DaemonPods("x", new(), false, dojoNodes));
hints: Reuse your matchLabels logic against each node's labels.
Then filter out tainted nodes unless `toleratesNoSchedule`.
